dod_intent_evidence: DARPA SBIR Phase II award ($1,726,448, 2023) 'Exceeding Limits Beyond Ordinary Wearables (ELBOW)' explicitly funds monitoring warfighter health and readiness — see SBIR/STTR record section.
score_evidence: 'Patent-pending sensor fusion enables zero-drift tracking without jitter or foot-sliding and within 2 degrees error to lighthouse trackers' → lab_language_intensity

'The framework will be built on a smartphone and provides the flexibility to add any number of Bluetooth Low Energy wearable sensors...while maintaining low energy consumption' with zero mention of ATO/RMF/CMMC/ITAR across the entire abstract → deployment_awareness_absence
'Help Us Help You! Our mission is to make full body tracking fun for all ages' — product framed entirely around consumer users, not operators or CONOPS → operator_absence
no jobs data found → hiring_profile_skew set to 10 per instructions
2-3 employee team, 'Coming Soon' pre-manufacturing product page, single DARPA Phase II with a period-of-performance clock → stage_pressure

blind_spots.blind_spot: The Link's real-time WiFi/BLE/USB output architecture assumes a live host connection
blind_spots.operator_reality: A DDIL field environment denies the continuous BLE/WiFi link the Link depends on to stream sensor-fusion data to a host in real time — same failure mode as the 30fps crowd-detection case
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: product was engineered for indoor VR/gaming rooms with a phone or PC always in range
blind_spots.evidence_quote: The Link takes the data from all the connected Trackers in realtime, performs its own body-informed sensor fusion, and outputs it via Bluetooth, WiFi, or USB.

blind_spots.blind_spot: 18-hour battery life assumes nightly recharge access
blind_spots.operator_reality: An austere OCONUS site has no guaranteed daily recharge point; wearable health sensors need field battery logistics and spares planning that consumer USB-C charging cases don't address
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: battery spec is pitched as a consumer convenience win ('play all day'), not a sustainment requirement
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Play all day with over 18 hours of active battery life from the Tracker's 20 mAH cell and the Link's 220 mAH cell.

blind_spots.blind_spot: ELBOW abstract treats warfighter health monitoring as a pure ML/data-pipeline problem
blind_spots.operator_reality: Any DoD-network deployment of a health-sensor smartphone framework needs ATO/RMF sign-off and likely CMMC compliance before it can touch government systems, plus training/sustainment for the E-5 wearing it
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: the abstract is written from a research-differentiation angle (IMU pose data vs. camera pose data) with no compliance or fielding section at all
blind_spots.evidence_quote: The framework will be built on a smartphone and provides the flexibility to add any number of Bluetooth Low Energy wearable sensors and/or internal smartphone sensors while maintaining low energy consumption.

opener_hook: Your DARPA ELBOW Phase II award funds a smartphone-based framework for monitoring warfighter health and readiness via wearable IMU sensors — built on the same real-time BLE/WiFi architecture as your consumer VR trackers.
what_they_do: Wearable IMU-based full-body motion-capture sensors built for VR/gaming/fitness, now extending via a DARPA SBIR into warfighter health and readiness monitoring.
